spec.title: Agent hooks through a real harness wrapper (PROP-064) — selection, consent, both modes, parking

p.purpose: **Purpose.** The Linux fixture `crates/vibe-cli/tests/cli_app_agents.rs` proves the hook contract with a fake agent. What it cannot prove is that a real harness, started from the presets as data, reads the prompt, works in the step's directory and answers: an attended Claude Code session in the terminal, the same harness in print mode, and the consent question a person actually answers. The owner proves these here with `~/opt/bin/claude-codex`, a launcher that starts Claude Code against another gateway and passes every argument through unchanged, so it is the `claude-code` preset with a different `command` (`PROP-064#acceptance`).

p.isolation-note: Every step runs against an isolated settings root (`VIBE_SETTINGS`) and a throw-away local registry. The agent runs with the user's authority in the installation work directory under that root; the demo prompt only writes one file there.

facts.PRE-HOST: Linux with an interactive terminal; `~/opt/bin/claude-codex` runs and reaches its gateway (`~/opt/bin/claude-codex -p "say hi"` prints an answer).

section.title: Setup
section.fence:
export VIBE_SETTINGS="$(mktemp -d)/vibe-mt06"; mkdir -p "$VIBE_SETTINGS" vibe=<checkout>/target/debug/vibe reg="$(mktemp -d)/registry"; pkg="$reg/org.example/hooked/v1.0.0"; mkdir -p "$pkg/bin" printf '#!/bin/sh\necho hooked\n' > "$pkg/bin/hooked" cat > "$pkg/vibe.toml" <<'TOML' [package] name = "hooked" group = "org.example" kind = "app" version = "1.0.0"
[application] id = "hooked"
[[installer_options]] id = "main" name = "Main" platform = "linux" platform_name = "Linux" arch = "x86_64"
[[installer_options.steps]] id = "payload" title = "Lay out the payload" kind = "copy" from = "bin" to = "bin"
[[installer_options.steps]] id = "fix" title = "Let an agent write a note into the payload" kind = "agent" prompt = """ Create the file $out/NOTE.txt containing one line that names today's date. Then write {"status": "ok", "message": "note written"} to the file named by the VIBE_HOOK_RUN environment variable plus /result.json, and stop. """ TOML sed -i "s/x86_64/$(uname -m)/" "$pkg/vibe.toml"

section.title: Steps

facts.STEP-1-NONE: **Without an agent the step is skipped and announced.**

p.EXP-1: **Expected.** Step 2 reads `skip (no agent configured) fix (agent)` and a closing `warning:` line names `fix` and the three ways to provide an agent (`--agent NAME`, `VIBE_AGENT_COMMAND`, `default` in agents.toml).

facts.STEP-2-REGISTER: **The wrapper is registered as a `claude-code` preset with its own command.**

section.fence: $vibe agent presets $vibe agent add claude-codex --preset claude-code --command ~/opt/bin/claude-codex --default $vibe agent list; cat "$VIBE_SETTINGS/agents.toml" $vibe app plan org.example/hooked --registry "$reg"

p.EXP-2: **Expected.** `presets` lists the six harnesses with their two templates. `list` shows `claude-codex [default] (preset claude-code)` with `interactive: …/claude-codex {prompt}` and `unattended: …/claude-codex -p {prompt}`; `agents.toml` starts with `default = "claude-codex"` and holds an `[agent.claude-codex]` table. The plan now reads `run fix (agent)` without a warning.

p.EXP-3: **Expected.** Before any step, the terminal shows `agent step `fix` (…) will run agent `claude-codex``, the command line with `{prompt}` and the full expanded prompt (with the real `$out` path), then asks `Run agent `claude-codex` with the prompt of step `fix`?`. Answering no ends with `needs consent` and exit 2; no work directory exists.

facts.STEP-4-INTERACTIVE: **Interactive: the harness takes over the terminal.**

section.fence: $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" # answer "yes"; let Claude Code do the task, then /exit echo "exit=$?"; cat "$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/apps/hooked/org.example.hooked@1.0.0/bin/NOTE.txt"

p.EXP-4: **Expected.** Claude Code opens in the terminal with the prompt already submitted, working in `…/cache/app-work/org.example.hooked@1.0.0`. After it writes the note and `result.json` and the session is closed, vibe prints `agent step `fix`: ok — note written`, places the payload and exits 0. `bin/NOTE.txt` is in the installed payload. Ctrl-C during the session ends it and the step is recorded `interrupted` (rerun with `--resume`).

section.fence: $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" --unattended $vibe app runs org.example/hooked ls "$(ls -d "$VIBE_SETTINGS"/cache/app-runs/org.example.hooked@1.0.0/* | tail -1)/steps/fix"

p.EXP-5: **Expected.** The prompt is shown but no question is asked (`--unattended` implies `--assume-yes`); `claude-codex -p …` output streams live; the install exits 0. The newest run record's `steps/fix/` holds `prompt.md`, `context.json` (`"protocol": "vibe-agent-hook/1"`, `"mode": "unattended"`), `transcript.log` with the harness's answer, `result.json` and `output.log`; its `steps.json` records the step `done` with `"agent": {"agent": "claude-codex", "mode": "unattended", "status": "ok", …}`.

facts.STEP-6-PARK: **Inside a hosting agent the task is parked, then resumed.** Run this from a terminal session of the hosting harness itself, or force it with `--agent-mode agent`.

section.fence: $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" --agent-mode agent; echo "exit=$?" # perform the printed task by hand, as the hosting agent would: work="$VIBE_SETTINGS/cache/app-work/org.example.hooked@1.0.0" date > "$work/out/NOTE.txt" echo '{"status":"ok","message":"done by the host"}' > "$work/steps/fix/result.json" $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" --agent-mode agent --resume; echo "exit=$?"

p.EXP-6: **Expected.** The first command starts no agent, prints one fenced `vibe-agent-tasks` block naming the run, the task file `…/agentic/outbox/<run>/fix.md` and the exact `resume:` command, and exits 75. The task file holds the prompt, the context and the answer contract. After the answer is written, `--resume` validates it, skips the already done `payload` step, finishes and exits 0.

facts.STEP-7-EXTERNAL: **An external registration wins over the default; `--agent` wins over both.**

section.fence: VIBE_AGENT_COMMAND=/bin/echo VIBE_AGENT_ARGS='["registered"]' $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" --unattended; echo "exit=$?" VIBE_AGENT_COMMAND=/bin/echo $vibe install -g org.example/hooked --registry "$reg" --unattended --agent claude-codex; echo "exit=$?"

p.EXP-7: **Expected.** The first run shows agent `external` and prints `registered --hook fix --mode unattended --prompt-file … --context-file … --work …` (`echo` exits 0 and writes no result, so the step is done without a message). The second run uses `claude-codex` again.

p.pass-criteria: Every step reads as described with the real wrapper: the announced skip, registration over a preset, the declined prompt with nothing run, an attended Claude Code session that answers through `result.json`, print mode with the transcript in the run record, parking with exit 75 and a validated `--resume`, and the selection order. The owner signs the date below.
